arXiv:1112.5707v1 [nlin.PS] 24 Dec 2011

Solitary and periodic solutions of the generalized Kuramoto - Sivashinsky equation

Nikolai A. Kudryashov
Department of Applied Mathematics
Moscow Engineering and Physics Institute
(State university)
31 Kashirskoe Shosse, 115409
Moscow, Russian Federation
Abstract

The generalized Kuramoto - Sivashinsky in the case of the power nonlinearity with arbitrary degree is considered. New exact solutions of this equation are presented.

Keywords: Exact solution, nonlinear differential equation, Kuramoto - Sivashinsky equation

PACS: 02.30.Hq - Ordinary differential equations

1 Introduction

In this paper we present exact solutions of the generalized Kuramoto - Sivashinsky equation

ut+um​ux+α​ux​x+β​ux​x​x+γ​ux​x​x​x=0\begin{gathered}u_{t}+u^{m}\,u_{x}+\alpha\,u_{xx}+\beta\,u_{xxx}+\gamma\,u_{xxxx}=0\end{gathered} (1.1)

Nonlinear evolution equation (1.1) at m=1m=1 has been studied by a number of authors from various viewpoints. This equation has drown much attention not only because it is interesting as a simple one - dimensional nonlinear evolution equation including effects of instability, dissipation and dispersion but also it is important for description in engineering and scientific problems. Equation (1.1) in work [1] was used for explanation of the origin of persistent wave propagation through medium of reaction - diffusion type. In paper [2] equation (1.1) was obtained at m=1m=1 for description of the nonlinear evolution of the disturbed flame front. We can meet the application of equation (1.1) for studying of motion of a viscous incompressible flowing down an inclined plane [3, 4, 5]. Mathematical model for consideration dissipative waves in plasma physics by means of equation (1.1) was presented in [6]. Elementary particles as solutions of the Kuramoto - Sivashinsky equation were studied in [7]. Equation (1.1) at m≠1m\neq 1 also can be used for the description of physical applications. For a example this equation were derived for description of nonlinear long waves in viscous - elastic tube [8].

Exact solution of equation (2.2) in the form of the solitary wave at m=1m=1 and at β=0\beta=0 were obtained in [1, 9]. Solitary wave solutions of equation (2.2) at m=1m=1 in the case β≠0\beta\neq 0 were found in works [10, 11, 12] for cases:

α=β216​γα=47​β2144​γ,α=73​β2256​γ.\begin{gathered}\alpha=\frac{\beta^{2}}{16\,\gamma}\quad\alpha=\frac{47\,\beta^{2}}{144\,\gamma},\quad\alpha=\frac{73\,\beta^{2}}{256\,\gamma}.\end{gathered} (1.2)

Other forms of these solutions were presented in works [13, 14, 15, 16, 17]. Periodical solutions of equation (2.2) were found in [18, 19] at α=β216​γ\alpha=\frac{\beta^{2}}{16\,\gamma}.

Exact solutions of equation (2.2) at m=2m=2 recently were obtained [8] for the four cases:

α=2​β225​γα=71​β2225​γ,α=121​β255​γ,α=374​β22025​γ.\begin{gathered}\alpha=\frac{2\,\beta^{2}}{25\,\gamma}\quad\alpha=\frac{71\,\beta^{2}}{225\,\gamma},\quad\alpha=\frac{121\,\beta^{2}}{55\,\gamma},\quad\alpha=\frac{374\,\beta^{2}}{2025\,\gamma}.\end{gathered} (1.3)

The aim of this paper is to search for exact solutions of equation (1.1) in general case of arbitrary degree mm. We present exact solutions of equation (1.1) at m≠−1m\neq-1, m≠−3m\neq-3 and m≠0m\neq 0. Some of these solutions are new.

2 Solitary waves of equation (1.1)

Using traveling wave

u⁡(x,t)=w⁡(z),z=x−C0​t\begin{gathered}u(x,t)=w(z),\,\qquad z=x-C_{0}\,t\end{gathered} (2.1)

from equation (1.1) we have

wz​z​z+σ​wz​z+wz−C0​w+1m+1​wm+1=0,m≠−1\begin{gathered}w_{zzz}+\sigma\,w_{zz}+w_{z}-C_{0}\,w+\frac{1}{m+1}\,w^{m+1}=0,\qquad m\neq-1\end{gathered} (2.2)

Assuming in (2.2)

w⁡(z)=v​(z)1m\begin{gathered}w(z)=v(z)^{\frac{1}{m}}\end{gathered} (2.3)

we have equation in the form

γ​m3​v2​vz​z​z+γ​m2​v2​vz​z​z+3​γ​m​v​vz​vz​z+β​m3​v2​vz​z−2​γ​m​vz3−−3​γ​m3​v​vz​vz​z+γ​vz3−γ​m2​vz3+2​γ​m3​vz3+β​m​v​vz2−−β​m3​v​vz2+β​m2​v2​vz​z+α​m3​v2​vz+α​m2​v2​vz+m3​v4−−C0​m4​v3−C0​m3​v3=0\begin{gathered}\gamma\,{m}^{3}\,{v}^{2}\,v_{{{zzz}}}+\gamma\,{m}^{2}\,{v}^{2}\,v_{{{zzz}}}+3\,\gamma\,m\,v\,v_{{z}}\,v_{{{zz}}}+\beta\,{m}^{3}\,{v}^{2}\,v_{{{zz}}}-2\,\gamma\,m\,{v_{{z}}}^{3}-\\ \\ -3\,\gamma\,{m}^{3}v\,v_{{z}}\,v_{{{zz}}}+\gamma\,{v_{{z}}}^{3}-\gamma\,{m}^{2}\,{v_{{z}}}^{3}+2\,\gamma\,{m}^{3}\,{v_{{z}}}^{3}+\beta\,m\,v\,{v_{{z}}}^{2}-\\ \\ -\beta\,{m}^{3}\,v\,{v_{{z}}}^{2}+\beta\,{m}^{2}\,{v}^{2}\,v_{{{zz}}}+\alpha\,{m}^{3}\,{v}^{2}\,v_{{z}}+\alpha\,{m}^{2}\,{v}^{2}\,v_{{z}}+{m}^{3}\,{v}^{4}-\\ \\ -{C_{0}}\,{m}^{4}\,{v}^{3}-{C_{0}}\,{m}^{3}\,{v}^{3}=0\end{gathered} (2.4)

Study of analytical properties of equation (2.4) allows us to determine that in the general case the meromorphic solutions of equation (2.4) can be found taking into account two cases:

α=β2​mγ​(m+3)2,α=β2​(2​m2+18​m+27)9​γ​(m+3)2\begin{gathered}\alpha={\frac{{\beta}^{2}\,m\,}{\gamma\left(m+3\right)^{2}}},\qquad\alpha=\,{\frac{{\beta}^{2}\,\left(2\,{m}^{2}+18\,m+27\right)\,}{9\,\gamma\left(m+3\right)^{2}}}\end{gathered} (2.5)

Consider the first case. The pole order of the solution of equation (2.4) is equal to three therefore we look for exact solutions of equation (2.4) in the form

v⁡(z)=A0+A1​Y​(z)+A2​Y​(z)2+A3​Y​(z)3,\begin{gathered}v(z)=A_{0}+A_{1}\,Y(z)+A_{2}\,Y(z)^{2}+A_{3}\,Y(z)^{3},\end{gathered} (2.6)

where Y⁡(z)Y(z) is solution of equation with the first order pole. Let us take simplest equation in the form [20, 21]

Yz=−Y2+b.\begin{gathered}Y_{z}=-Y^{2}+b.\end{gathered} (2.7)

Substituting (2.6) into (2.4) and taking into account equation (2.7) we have

b=β2​m24​γ2​(m+3)2.\begin{gathered}b\,=\,{\frac{{\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}}{4\,{\gamma}^{2}\left(m+3\right)^{2}}}.\end{gathered} (2.8)

We have also the following values of coefficients in (2.6)

A3=3​γ​(2​m+3)​(m+3)​(m+1)m3,A2=−3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)​β2​m2,A1=−3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)​β24​(m+3)​m​γ,C0=2​(m+2)​β3γ2​(m+3)3,A0=3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)​β38​γ2​(m+3)2.\begin{gathered}A_{{3}}={\frac{3\,\gamma\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)}{{m}^{3}}},\\ \\ A_{{2}}=-\,{\frac{3\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)\beta}{2\,{m}^{2}}},\quad A_{{1}}=-\,{\frac{3\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right){\beta}^{2}}{4\,\left(m+3\right)m\,\gamma}},\\ \\ C_{{0}}=\,{\frac{2\,\left(m+2\right){\beta}^{3}}{{\gamma}^{2}\left(m+3\right)^{3}}},\quad A_{0}=\,{\frac{3\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right){\beta}^{3}}{{8\,\gamma}^{2}\left(m+3\right)^{2}}}.\end{gathered} (2.9)

We have solutions of equation (2.7) in the form

Y(z)=β​m2​γ​(m+3)tanh{β​m​(z−z0)2​γ​(m+3)}.\begin{gathered}Y(z)\,=\,\frac{\beta\,m}{2\,{\gamma}\,\left(m+3\right)}\,\,\tanh\left\{\,{\frac{\beta\,m\,\left(z-{z_{0}}\right)}{2\,\gamma\,\left(m+3\right)}}\right\}.\end{gathered} (2.10)

Solution of equation (2.2) takes the form

w⁡(z)=(3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)​β38​γ​(m+3))1m​(1−tanh⁡{β​m​(z−z0)2​γ​(m+3)})2m(1+tanh⁡{β​m​(z−z0)2​γ​(m+3)})1m,m≠0,m≠−3,m≠−1.\begin{gathered}w(z)=\left(\frac{3\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right){\beta}^{3}}{8\,\gamma\,\left(m+3\right)}\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}\,\,\left(1-\tanh\left\{{\frac{\beta\,m\,\left(z-{z_{0}}\right)}{2\,\gamma\left(m+3\right)}}\right\}\right)^{\frac{2}{m}}\\ \left(1+\tanh\left\{{\frac{\beta\,m\,\left(z-{z_{0}}\right)}{2\,\gamma\left(m+3\right)}}\right\}\right)^{\frac{1}{m}},\quad m\neq 0,\quad m\neq-3,\quad m\neq-1.\end{gathered} (2.11)

This is new solution of equation (1.1). Solution (2.11) at m=1m=1 takes the form of the solitary wave that was obtained in [10]. In the case m=2m=2 this solution corresponds to exact solution of equation (1.1) published in [8].

Consider the second case. Solutions of equation (2.4) we look for taking into consideration the transformation (2.6) again. Function Y⁡(z)Y(z) satisfies equation (2.8) as well. In this case we obtain the expression for the parameter bb in the form

b=β2​m236​γ2​(m+3)2.\begin{gathered}b\,=\,{\frac{{\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}}{36\,{\gamma}^{2}\,\left(m+3\right)^{2}}}.\end{gathered} (2.12)

We also obtain coefficients A3A_{3}, A2A_{2}, A1A_{1}, C0C_{0} and A0A_{0} as following

A3=3​γ​(2​m+3)​(m+3)​(m+1)m3,A2=−3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)​β2​m2,A1=(2​m+3)​(m+1)​β24​γ​m​(m+3),C0=−(2​m+3)​β39​(m+3)2​γ2,A0=−β3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)72​(m+3)2​γ2.\begin{gathered}A_{{3}}=\,{\frac{3\,\gamma\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)}{{m}^{3}}},\\ \\ A_{{2}}=-\,{\frac{3\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)\beta}{2\,\,{m}^{2}}},\quad A_{{1}}=\,{\frac{\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right){\beta}^{2}}{4\,\gamma\,m\,\left(m+3\right)}},\\ \\ C_{{0}}=-\,{\frac{\left(2\,m+3\right){\beta}^{3}}{9\,\left(m+3\right)^{2}{\gamma}^{2}}},\quad A_{{0}}=-\,{\frac{{\beta}^{3}\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)}{72\,\left(m+3\right)^{2}{\gamma}^{2}}}.\end{gathered} (2.13)

Using these coefficients we have solution of equation (2.2). It takes the form

w⁡(z)=(β3​(2​m+3)​(m+1)72​γ2​(m+3)2)1m​(tanh⁡{β​m​(z−z0)6​γ​(m+3)}−1)3m,m≠0,m≠−1,m≠−3.\begin{gathered}w(z)=\left({\frac{{\beta}^{3}\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\,\left(m+1\right)}{72\,\gamma^{2}\,\left(m+3\right)^{2}\,}}\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}\,\left(\tanh\left\{{\frac{\beta\,m\,\left(z-{z_{0}}\right)}{6\,\gamma\,\left(m+3\right)}}\right\}-1\right)^{\frac{3}{m}},\\ \\ m\neq 0,\quad m\neq-1,\quad m\neq-3.\end{gathered} (2.14)

Other forms of this solution were found in works [22, 23, 24]. At m=1m=1 from (2.14) we have one of the solitary solutions of work [10]. In the case m=2m=2 we get solution [8].

3 Periodical waves of equation (1.1)

Let us find periodical solutions of equation (2.2) taking into consideration the formula [18]

w(z)=A0+A1R+A2Rz,R≡R(z),\begin{gathered}w(z)=A_{0}+A_{1}\,R+A_{2}\,R_{z},\qquad R\equiv R(z),\end{gathered} (3.1)

taking into account the relation for the parameter α\alpha

α=β2​mγ​(m+3)2.\begin{gathered}\alpha\,=\,{\frac{{\beta}^{2}\,m}{\gamma\left(m+3\right)^{2}}}.\end{gathered} (3.2)

We assume that R⁡(z)R(z) is solution of equation for the Weierstrass function

Rz​z+6​R2−a​R−b=0\begin{gathered}R_{{{zz}}}+6\,{R}^{2}-a\,R-b=0\end{gathered} (3.3)

From equation (3.3) we have equation

Rz2+4​R3−a​R2−2​b​R+d=0\begin{gathered}R_{{{z}}}^{2}+4\,{R}^{3}-a\,R^{2}-2\,b\,R+d=0\end{gathered} (3.4)

Substituting (3.1) into equation (2.3) and taking into account equations (3.3) and (3.4) we have

b=m4​β4−γ4​a2​(m+3)224​γ4​(m+3)4,A2==3​γ​(2​m+3)​(m+3)​(m+1)2​m3,A1=3​β​(2​m+3)​(m+1)2​m2,C0=2​β3​(m+2)γ2​(m+3)3,A0=β⁡(2​m+3)​(m+1)​(β2​m2−γ2​(m+3)2​a)8​γ2​m2​(m+3)2,\begin{gathered}b=\,{\frac{{m}^{4}{\beta}^{4}-\gamma^{4}\,a^{2}\,\left(m+3\right)^{2}\,}{{24\,\gamma}^{4}\left(m+3\right)^{4}}},\quad A_{2}==\,{\frac{3\,\gamma\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)}{2\,{m}^{3}}},\\ \\ A_{{1}}=\,{\frac{3\,\beta\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\left(m+1\right)}{2\,{m}^{2}}},\quad C_{0}=\,{\frac{2\,{\beta}^{3}\,\left(m+2\right)}{{\gamma}^{2}\left(m+3\right)^{3}}},\\ \\ A_{0}=\,{\frac{\beta\,\left(2\,m+3\right)\,\left(m+1\right)\,\left({\beta}^{2}\,{m}^{2}-{\gamma}^{2}\,({m+3})^{2}\,a\,\right)}{{8\,\gamma}^{2}{m}^{2}\left(m+3\right)^{2}}},\end{gathered} (3.5)
d=(2​β2​m2+γ2​(m+3)2​a)​(β2​m2−γ2​(m+3)2​a)2432​γ6​(m+3)6\begin{gathered}d=\,{\frac{\left(2\,{\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}+{\gamma}^{2}\,(m+3)^{2}\,a\,\right)\,\left({\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}-{\gamma}^{2}\,{(m+3)}^{2}\,a\,\right)^{2}}{432\,\,{\gamma}^{6}\left(m+3\right)^{6}}}\end{gathered} (3.6)

Solution of equation (2.2) in this case takes the form

w⁡(z)=(3​(m+1)​(2​m+3)2​m2)1m(β​R​(z)+γ⁡(m+3)m​Rz+β⁡(β2​m2−γ2​(m+3)2​a)12​γ2​(m+3)2)1m,\begin{gathered}w(z)=\left(\frac{3\,\left(m+1\right)\,\left(2\,m+3\right)}{2\,{m}^{2}}\,\right)^{\frac{1}{m}}\\ \left(\beta\,R\left(z\right)+{\frac{\gamma\left(m+3\right)}{m}}\,R_{z}+\,{\frac{\beta\,\left({\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}-{\gamma}^{2}\,\left(m+3\right)^{2}a\,\right)}{12\,{\gamma}^{2}\left(m+3\right)^{2}}}\right)^{\frac{1}{m}},\end{gathered} (3.7)

where R⁡(z)R(z) satisfies equation

Rz2+4​R3−a​R2−(m4​β4−γ4​a2​(m+3)4)12​γ4​(m+3)4​R−−(2​β2​m2+γ2​(m+3)2​a)​(β2​m2−γ2​(m+3)2​a)2432​γ6​(m+3)6=0\begin{gathered}{R_{{z}}}^{2}+4\,{R}^{3}-a\,{R}^{2}-\,{\frac{\left({m}^{4}{\beta}^{4}-{\gamma}^{4}\,{a}^{2}\,\left(m+3\right)^{4}\right)}{12\,{\gamma}^{4}\left(m+3\right)^{4}}}\,\,R-\\ \\ -\,{\frac{\left(2\,{\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}+{\gamma}^{2}\,(m+3)^{2}\,a\,\right)\,\left({\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}-{\gamma}^{2}\,{(m+3)}^{2}\,a\,\right)^{2}}{432\,\,{\gamma}^{6}\left(m+3\right)^{6}}}=0\end{gathered} (3.8)

In general case solutions of equation (3.8) expressed via hyperbolic function because the algebraic equation

4​R3−a​R2−(m4​β4−γ4​a2​(m+3)4)12​γ4​(m+3)4​R−(2​β2​m2+γ2​(m+3)2​a)​(β2​m2−γ2​(m+3)2​a)2432​γ6​(m+3)6=0\begin{gathered}4\,{R}^{3}-a\,{R}^{2}-\,{\frac{\left({m}^{4}{\beta}^{4}-{\gamma}^{4}\,{a}^{2}\,\left(m+3\right)^{4}\right)}{12\,{\gamma}^{4}\left(m+3\right)^{4}}}\,\,R-\\ \\ \,{\frac{\left(2\,{\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}+{\gamma}^{2}\,(m+3)^{2}\,a\,\right)\,\left({\beta}^{2}{m}^{2}-{\gamma}^{2}\,{(m+3)}^{2}\,a\,\right)^{2}}{432\,\,{\gamma}^{6}\left(m+3\right)^{6}}}=0\end{gathered} (3.9)

has two equal roots.

However there are periodic solutions of equation (1.1) at m=1m=1 and m=3m=3. Parameter C0C_{0} in these cases will be arbitrary constant. Other coefficients can be found from expressions (3.5). Let us present these solutions using formula (3.1).

In the case m=1m=1 we have α=β216​γ\alpha=\frac{\beta^{2}}{16\,\gamma}. Solution of equation (1.1) takes the form [18]

y⁡(z)=C0−54​β​a−164​β3γ2+15​β​R+60​γ​Rz\begin{gathered}y(z)={C_{0}}-\frac{5}{4}\,\beta\,a-{\frac{1}{64}}\,{\frac{{\beta}^{3}}{{\gamma}^{2}}}+15\,\beta\,\,R+60\,\gamma\,\,{R_{z}}\end{gathered} (3.10)

where R⁡(z)R(z) satisfies equation for the Weierstrass function

Rz2+4​R3−a​R2−2​(β46144​γ4−a224)​R++13​β64423680​γ6+a​β436864​γ4−C022160​γ2−a3432=0\begin{gathered}{R_{{z}}}^{2}+4\,{R}^{3}-a{R}^{2}-2\,\left(\,{\frac{{\beta}^{4}}{6144\,{\gamma}^{4}}}-\frac{{a}^{2}}{24}\,\right)R+\\ \\ +{\frac{13\,{\beta}^{6}}{4423680\,\gamma^{6}}}\,+\,\,{\frac{a\,{\beta}^{4}}{{36864\,\gamma}^{4}}}-\,{\frac{{C_{{0}}}^{2}}{2160\,{\gamma}^{2}}}-{\frac{{a}^{3}}{432}}\,=0\end{gathered} (3.11)

In the case m=3m=3 we have α=β212​γ\alpha=\frac{\beta^{2}}{12\,\gamma}. Periodic solution of equation (1.1) in this case can be written in the form

y⁡(z)=(3​C0−12​β​a−172​β3γ2+6​β​R+12​γ​Rz)13\begin{gathered}y(z)=\left(3\,{C_{0}}-\frac{1}{2}\,\beta\,a-{\frac{1}{72}}\,{\frac{{\beta}^{3}}{{\gamma}^{2}}}+6\,\beta\,R+12\,\gamma\,R_{{z}}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\end{gathered} (3.12)

where R⁡(z)R(z) satisfies equation for the Weierstrass function in the form

Rz2+4​R3−a​R2−2​(C0​β8​γ2−11​β43456​γ4−a224)​R−−11​β4​a20736​γ4+13​β6373248​γ6+C0​β31728​γ4+C0​β​a48​γ2−C0216​γ2−a3432=0\begin{gathered}{R_{{z}}}^{2}+4\,{R}^{3}-a\,{R}^{2}-2\,\left(\,{\frac{C_{{0}}\beta}{8\,{\gamma}^{2}}}-{\frac{11\,{\beta}^{4}}{3456\,{\gamma}^{4}}}-\frac{{a}^{2}}{24}\,\right)R-\\ \\ -{\frac{11\,{\beta}^{4}a}{20736\,{\gamma}^{4}}}+{\frac{13\,{\beta}^{6}}{373248\,{\gamma}^{6}}}+{\frac{C_{{0}}{\beta}^{3}}{{1728\,\gamma}^{4}}}+{\frac{C_{{0}}\beta\,a}{48\,{\gamma}^{2}}}-{\frac{{C_{{0}}}^{2}}{16\,{\gamma}^{2}}}-{\frac{{a}^{3}}{432}}\,=0\end{gathered} (3.13)

This solution of equation (1.1) is a new. Let us note that periodical solutions of equation (1.1) are appeared at m=1m=1 and at m=3m=3 when there is meromorphic solutions in the form of solitary waves of equation (1.1).
